clue.text: Not happy with the vinaigrette, gave a severe reprimand

parts.note: vinaigrette is a salad dressing
feeling down means feeling low, unhappy

explanation.surface: A diner unhappy with the salad dressing gave the waiter a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces and 'gave' is a link word; the vinaigrette's piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is an idiom for a sharp scolding.

clue.text: Set a target for race meeting

indicators.note: to set something can mean to arrange or put it in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Organisers fix a goal for an upcoming sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' reads as a verb meaning fix, but it tells you to rearrange A TARGET.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races held as one event.

clue.text: What type of leather has changed colour?

indicators.note: the word has, once changed, is a reshuffled set of its own letters

parts.note: green is a colour

explanation.surface: A question about which hide has been dyed a different shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns HAS into SHA; GREEN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is untanned leather with a granular surface, often dyed green.

clue.text: Cold one caught on head reguarly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: regularly (as printed, misspelt) means take every other letter of the word head

explanation.surface: Someone keeps catching a chill on their head again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of HEAD give ED; 'on' joins the pieces in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means chilled, made very cold.

clue.text: Be sacked at the butcher's request

definitions.meaning: a customer asking a butcher for a cut of meat might ask to have a chop

explanation.surface: Someone loses their job in a butcher's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the chop is slang for dismissal, and literally what a butcher's customer may want.

clue.text: Start of spring — lost little weight

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for spring is the part dealt with
lost means that first letter is dropped from the word for spring

parts.note: to spring is to bounce

explanation.surface: At the beginning of the season a dieter shed a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' and 'lost' together take the B off BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Zeroes had better be found between poles

indicators.note: the word for had better must sit between the letters standing for the two poles

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
ought means had better, should

explanation.surface: Polar explorers would be wise to expect temperatures at freezing point.
explanation.definitionFit: Noughts are zeros, the figure 0.

clue.text: Gossips hid the dress — it was scruffy

indicators.note: something scruffy is untidy and messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone concealed a frock because it looked shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish the dirt is an idiom for spreading scandal, so one who does it gossips.

clue.text: The "L" in vehicle

parts.note: an L-plate on a car marks a novice motorist, so the person behind the wheel is what the letter stands for

explanation.surface: The letter L displayed on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a car driven by someone without a licence must carry red L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: L-plates mark a novice motorist still being taught.

clue.text: One's not happy where the fire is

definitions.meaning: an ungrateful person, someone never content with what is given
read as two words, inside the hearth's metal frame

explanation.surface: Someone sulks by the fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, and a fire burns in a grate.

clue.text: Head of religious order?

parts.note: not the abbot leading a community but the shaven crown on a monk's head

explanation.surface: Who leads a monastic community?
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved patch on the scalp of a monk or priest.

clue.text: One doesn't like to lose energy from radiator

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for energy is taken out of the word for radiator

parts.note: a radiator is a heater
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes how much power the heating wastes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater is someone who dislikes something strongly.

clue.text: One flails — it could be a shark

definitions.meaning: someone who beats grain with a flail to separate it
a long-tailed shark species shares the name

explanation.surface: A thrashing creature turns out to be a predator of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A thresher beats out grain, and the thresher shark is named for its whip-like tail.

clue.text: Stop, or go and join the others

definitions.meaning: read literally, go to the remainder of the group

explanation.surface: An instruction to halt or to rejoin the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to rest is to halt, and literally to come to the rest of the group.

clue.text: Transport offered by a drama teacher

parts.note: the stage is the world of drama
a coach is a teacher or trainer

explanation.surface: A lift home given by an acting tutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagecoach is a horse-drawn passenger vehicle of old.

clue.text: Man perhaps lives with life on the outside

parts.note: is means lives, exists

indicators.note: on the outside means take only the outside letters of the word life

explanation.surface: A man lives life as an outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island.

clue.text: Border hospital on suffering in battle

parts.note: an edge is a border
ill means sick, suffering

explanation.surface: A hospital at the frontier treats the wounded of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgehill (1642) was the first major battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgehill is a Warwickshire field where a famous Civil War battle was fought.

clue.text: The boss listened, dropping resistance

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for resistance falls out of the word for listened

parts.note: heard means listened to
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: The manager paid attention and stopped objecting.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an organisation is its boss.

clue.text: CIA bore broke down, demanding oxygen

indicators.note: something that broke down has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tedious intelligence agent collapsed, gasping for air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic exercise or organisms require oxygen.

clue.text: Used to see champion writing

parts.note: to second is to support or champion
hand means handwriting

explanation.surface: Someone wanted to watch a winner signing autographs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champion' looks like a noun but is the verb, to back; 'to see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been owned before, so they are pre-owned.

clue.text: Forgetting that men fight in the continent

indicators.note: in places the scrambled men inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: men who fight are thrown about, so their letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Wars on a far continent are soon put out of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fight' makes MNE from MEN, which goes inside ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory.

clue.text: Board member and corrupt creditor

indicators.note: something corrupt is rotten and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company official who is also a crooked lender.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on a company's board.

clue.text: Deranged scream about street map

indicators.note: about means the word for scream goes round the street map

parts.note: a cry is a scream
an A-Z is a book of street maps in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks wildly while holding a town map.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a British street atlas, named for its alphabetical index.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy means mad, out of one's mind.

clue.text: Even Nehru emptied one in boredom

indicators.note: emptied means the insides of both words are removed, leaving their outside letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Even India's first prime minister found himself weary and listless.
explanation.walkthrough: Emptying EVEN and NEHRU leaves EN and NU; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, tedium.

clue.text: Spoken alternative to 9

annotationWithheld.why: Spoken alternative to 9 (4): 9 is LEARNER DRIVER, and OR (alternative) leaves AL unexplained by 'to 9'; no sound parse found, the cross-reference may be wrong

clue.text: One's heart a prisoner to it

definitions.text: One's heart a prisoner to it

parts.words: One's heart a prisoner to it
parts.note: read literally, the heart sits locked behind bars of bone inside the chest

explanation.surface: Someone is lovestruck, their heart captive to another.
explanation.definitionFit: The ribs form a protective frame enclosing heart and lungs.

clue.text: Publication about contentious point

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an issue is a point in dispute

explanation.surface: A printed piece on a disputed topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a book or record published again.

clue.text: Rally cars etc are specially designed, that's obvious

indicators.note: letters specially designed are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: Motorsport vehicles are custom-built, as is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal-clear means perfectly plain and evident.
